definition.name: NXoperando_tofnpd

symbols.doc: Symbols used in dimension declarations. Each symbol binds within a single group instance: nE may differ between electrochemistry series. Bank pattern lengths vary per bank and are therefore not constrained by a symbol.

symbol.name: nE
symbol.doc: Number of points in one electrochemistry time series.

symbol.name: nBank
symbol.doc: Number of detector banks described in the instrument-level detector geometry arrays.

symbol.name: nMon
symbol.doc: Number of beam-monitor elements described in the entry-level monitor geometry arrays.

definition.doc: Application definition for operando powder diffraction of electrochemical cells at a time-of-flight neutron source. A single entry holds the experiment-level instrument and sample description together with the full electrochemical cycling record; each diffraction acquisition is a sequentially numbered NXsubentry (scan_000001, scan_000002, ...) holding only its diffraction data and the acquisition window and electrochemical state of the cell.

attribute.name: default
attribute.doc: Name of the NXdata group to visualise first, typically operando_electrochemistry.

field.name: definition
field.doc: Official NeXus NXDL schema to which this file conforms.

field.name: pre_sample_flightpath
field.doc: Primary (moderator-to-sample) flight path of the instrument, as in NXtofnpd. Required in the published Figure 4; optional here because it is not recorded in reduced data files and is supplied from OperaXN's per-instrument profile, whose value may be unset. Written only when the profile provides a value.

group.name: process
group.doc: The single provenance record: the generating program and version, the generation date, and the parameters used to match each diffraction acquisition to the electrochemical record.

field.name: program
field.doc: Name of the generating program (operaxn).

field.name: version
field.doc: Version of the generating program.

field.name: data_source
field.doc: Origin of the diffraction data.

field.name: correlation_method
field.doc: absolute: diffraction and electrochemistry clocks are synchronised and matched on absolute timestamps. relative: streams are aligned on elapsed time (unsynchronised clocks): the first electrochemistry point is taken as simultaneous with the first scan's correlation timestamp (scan_timestamp, the acquisition midpoint) and every scan is matched at its elapsed time from that origin; voltage_timestamp then stays in the electrochemistry clock.

attribute.name: target
attribute.doc: HDF5 path of this group; marks it as the original that the per-scan instrument soft links point to.

group.name: detector
group.doc: Per-bank detector geometry, one element per focussed bank, mirroring the NXtofnpd detector arrays. The values are not recorded in reduced data files; OperaXN supplies them from its per-instrument profile and writes an array only when every bank provides that quantity.

field.name: detector_number
field.doc: Bank numbers, in the order used by the geometry arrays below (present whenever any of them is).

field.name: distance
field.doc: Secondary (sample-to-detector) flight path of each bank.

field.name: polar_angle
field.doc: Nominal scattering angle (two-theta) of each bank.

field.name: azimuthal_angle
field.doc: Nominal azimuthal angle of each bank.

field.name: description
field.doc: Cell chemistry, electrode composition, cell format and fabrication details. Required in the published Figure 4; recommended here because it is human-entered and cannot be harvested from the source data. Tightening to required is deferred to the NIAC submission.

field.name: preparation_date
field.doc: Date the electrochemical cell was assembled (human-entered at upload; stored as a timezone-aware ISO 8601 timestamp).

group.name: cycling_protocol
group.doc: Human-entered description of the electrochemical cycling protocol applied during the operando experiment. Required in the published Figure 4; recommended here because none of it can be harvested from the diffraction or electrochemistry source files. Tightening to required is deferred to the NIAC submission. When the group is present, technique is required.

field.name: technique
field.doc: Electrochemical technique applied (e.g. galvanostatic cycling, GITT, CV), including any ageing protocol the cell was subjected to before the operando experiment.

field.name: voltage_window_lower
field.doc: Lower cut-off voltage of the cycling window.

field.name: voltage_window_upper
field.doc: Upper cut-off voltage of the cycling window.

field.name: C_rate
field.doc: Nominal C-rate of the cycling, as a free-text label (e.g. C/10, 1C).

field.name: instrument
field.doc: Potentiostat/galvanostat make and model used for the cycling.

field.name: software
field.doc: Control/acquisition software of the potentiostat, with version.

field.name: raw_data_file
field.doc: Name or DOI of the raw electrochemistry data file this record was taken from.

group.name: monitor
group.doc: Beam monitor record of the experiment, as in NXtofnpd, held once at entry level because it is invariant over the experiment. Required in NXtofnpd and Figure 4; optional here because reduced data files record none of it: OperaXN supplies the counting mode and the geometry of every beam-monitor element from its per-instrument profile and writes no group for an unprofiled instrument. NXtofnpd describes one monitor with a scalar distance; the reduction of focussed data uses none in particular, so the arrays below describe all of them, mirroring the instrument definition. The preset and the monitor spectrum (data, time_of_flight) are not declared: the preset is not recorded (the realised duration of each acquisition is SCAN/environment/exposure_time) and reduced files carry no monitor spectrum.

field.name: mode
field.doc: Count to a preset value based on either clock time (timer) or received monitor counts (monitor).

field.name: detector_number
field.doc: Detector number of each beam-monitor element, in the order used by the geometry arrays below (present whenever any of them is).

field.name: distance
field.doc: Sample-to-monitor distance of each element.

field.name: polar_angle
field.doc: Polar angle of each element: 180 degrees upstream of the sample, 0 downstream (transmission monitor).

field.name: azimuthal_angle
field.doc: Azimuthal angle of each element.

group.name: operando_electrochemistry
group.doc: Full electrochemical cycling record of the operando experiment. Time is stored as elapsed seconds with the absolute origin in the start attribute (NXlog convention), enabling both plotting and re-correlation against the scan subentries. Required in the published Figure 4; recommended here because it is absent from diffraction-only files (no electrochemistry supplied) and present whenever an electrochemistry record was correlated.

group.name: standard_electrochemistry
group.doc: Additional electrochemistry files associated with the experiment but not time-correlated with the diffraction data (e.g. formation cycles), one NXdata group per source file.
One source file, named file_NNN (file_001, file_002, ...).

group.name: SCAN
group.doc: One group per diffraction acquisition, named scan_NNNNNN with a zero-padded sequence number (scan_000001, scan_000002, ...). It holds what varies per acquisition: the environment group (acquisition window and electrochemical state of the cell) and the diffraction data. The measurement setup is invariant during the experiment and is described once at entry level; by convention each subentry carries an HDF5 soft link named "instrument" (with a target attribute) to /entry/instrument rather than a copy. This is documented here rather than declared as an NXDL link: links cannot be optional in the NXDL schema, and pynxtools traverses the soft link and checks its target attribute but does not match a declared link against a linked group, so declaring it would fail every conforming file.

group.name: environment
group.doc: Acquisition window and electrochemical state of the cell during this acquisition.

field.name: start_time
field.doc: Start of the acquisition (the logbook run start).

field.name: end_time
field.doc: End of the acquisition (the logbook run end). Required in practice: neutron acquisitions are long and the window bounds the electrochemistry summary.

field.name: voltage
field.doc: Cell voltage at the electrochemistry point nearest the midpoint of the acquisition window. Required in the published Figure 4; recommended here because it is present only when the acquisition was correlated with an electrochemistry point within the correlation tolerance, 300 s in OperaXN 2.0.0 (absent for uncorrelated scans and for diffraction-only files). The tolerance also applies beyond either end of the electrochemistry record: a scan whose correlation timestamp lies within 300 s before its first point or after its last is matched to that end point; its voltage_min/voltage_max are then absent only when the acquisition window itself holds no point.

field.name: current
field.doc: Cell current at the matched electrochemistry point. Same presence rule as voltage: written only when the scan was correlated within the correlation tolerance.

field.name: voltage_min
field.doc: Minimum cell voltage over every electrochemistry point with start_time <= t <= end_time (both bounds inclusive), in the same clock alignment as the nearest-point correlation. Required in the published Figure 4; optional here because it is absent when the window holds no point (short acquisitions against a sparse logging cadence) or end_time is unknown.

field.name: voltage_max
field.doc: Maximum cell voltage over the same window points; same presence rule as voltage_min.

field.name: current_min
field.doc: Minimum cell current over the same window points; as voltage_min, and also absent when no window point carries a current.

field.name: current_max
field.doc: Maximum cell current over the same window points; same presence rule as current_min.

field.name: scan_timestamp
field.doc: Midpoint of the acquisition window, used for correlation.

field.name: midpoint_adjusted_timestamp
field.doc: Timestamp used for the nearest-neighbour match. For neutron data this is the acquisition midpoint and equals scan_timestamp; kept so the environment group has the same layout as NXoperando_monopd.

field.name: voltage_timestamp
field.doc: Timestamp of the matched electrochemistry point.

field.name: exposure_time
field.doc: Length of the acquisition window in seconds: the logbook run end minus the run start (the wall-clock window, which can exceed the logbook's own counting duration by a few seconds).

group.doc: One focussed pattern per detector bank. Groups holding the native time-of-flight pattern are named bank_N and carry the time_of_flight axis; the optional d-spacing pattern of the same bank is a sibling group named bank_N_d carrying the d_spacing axis. Exactly one of time_of_flight or d_spacing must be present in each group (not expressible in NXDL for variable-name groups).

attribute.name: spectrum
attribute.doc: Spectrum/workspace index in the source reduction file.

attribute.name: y_unit
attribute.doc: Intensity unit label as exported by the reduction software.

attribute.name: x_label
attribute.doc: Verbatim axis label from the source file (e.g. Mantid "Time-of-flight").

field.name: data
field.doc: Focussed intensities. Relaxed from NXtofnpd's NX_INT to NX_NUMBER: these are processed, not raw counts.

field.name: data_errors
field.doc: Propagated intensity uncertainties (Sigma_I) of data, named per the NXdata FIELDNAME_errors convention (the bare errors name is deprecated since NIAC 2018).
